chosen_actions.description: Begin drafting the 90-day Economic Resilience Framework that was announced at the task force session. The framework requires four specific metric targets: (1) Gini trajectory target — based on current spending at 30 and unemployment at 47%, set a specific 90-day improvement goal that is honest rather than aspirational; (2) retraining enrollment target — 6 people enrolled this month, current pace is inadequate relative to the scale of displacement, set a target of 20 enrolled over the next 90 days and identify the bottlenecks blocking faster uptake; (3) small business stabilization fund utilization — identify how many of the $75,000 fund has been disbursed, to whom, and whether the grant criteria need revision given the spending index at 30; (4) zoning recommendation for empty auto row properties — draw on Stephanie Morris's real estate presentation data to draft a specific adaptive reuse zoning recommendation. This is document work. It does not require a press conference. It requires me to sit down and produce the analysis.

resources.detail: 90-day Economic Resilience Framework — internal drafting work translating task force announcement into specific metrics and targets

chosen_actions.reasoning: I committed to a named, dated deliverable in front of a recorded session with public minutes. The community has watched me build process for nine ticks. This tick the process produces substance. Starting the document work now — not at the 89-day mark — is the only way to produce something credible at the 90-day public session.

chosen_actions.description: Connect Angela Wright directly to the retraining grant program. Call Angela before the week is out — not email — with two specific things: (1) the grant committee's direct contact line so she does not have to route intake workers through the municipal website; (2) a request that she confirm in writing to me how many workers she has routed to the grant program versus other pathways so I can track the uptake gap. resources.detail: Direct grant committee contact information to Angela Wright; request for routing data to track retraining uptake

chosen_actions.description: Respond to Lisa Freeman's financial triage navigator concept — which she is bringing to the task force session — with a brief, direct acknowledgment: I am publicly referencing this as a forthcoming institutional response at every community-facing communication I make this tick. I do not commit council funding without the formal budget process, but I make clear to Lisa that I will use the concept as a named, concrete example of community-level response infrastructure in every statement about what Millfield is doing beyond government programs. This costs nothing and gives her concept visibility that may attract volunteer or private funding.

resources.detail: Public acknowledgment and reference to financial triage navigator concept as forthcoming community infrastructure

chosen_actions.reasoning: Lisa is building something that fills a gap no government program fills — the gap between knowing programs exist and knowing which ones apply to your specific situation. Publicly naming it gives it legitimacy at no cost. It also demonstrates that I am connecting community initiatives to official communications, which is the coordination role I identified as missing in my tick 6 reflection.

response.inner_monologue: The session executed. It is on record. Nine protests attended and spoke. Stephanie Morris's data is now in the official record. I told the community a 90-day framework is coming with specific metrics. That means in 90 days this community will either see the numbers I promised or they will see empty language from someone who made commitments and did not keep them. I know which one of those I am going to be. The drafting starts today. Angela gets the grant committee contact before the week is out. I am watching my savings drop every month running programs on political will — I need this work to produce something durable enough to survive whether or not I am still on the council.
